response_json.request: Hi, Please create a filling system on the radiator, including a pouring section and a cap.

actions.relational_constraint: The pouring section must be included in the filling system located on the radiator.
actions.unresolved_reference: The original placement ambiguity is resolved to the center of the upper radiator header using F012 and FACE 798 as the existing filler-cap reference and FACE 46 as the cap-bearing header wall. Exact neck diameter, bore diameter, height, wall thickness, sealing standard, and retention interface remain unspecified and must be derived from the existing cap envelope or an engineering specification.
steps: Use the inferred semantic orientation with confidence 0.88: the +Y view is the top of the radiator. The multiview images show the filler or service cap centered on this upper header, confirming that the filling system belongs on the cap-bearing upper-header region rather than on the fan guards, core panels, or coolant hose fittings.

Localize the pouring section on R01, feature F001, using FACE 46, the planar upper-header outer wall at CAD y=174.851756 mm. Establish the pouring-section axis through the center of the existing F012 cap represented by SOLID 19 and FACE 798, approximately at CAD z=0, with the axis normal to FACE 46 and directed along +Y.

Temporarily suppress, hide, or remove SOLID 19 from the active boolean body while constructing the filler neck so that the existing cap does not obstruct the header cut or produce duplicate overlapping closure geometry. Preserve FACE 798 as the reference envelope for the mating neck and replacement or retained cap.

Create a sketch on FACE 46, or on a datum plane tangent and coincident with FACE 46, centered on the projected centroid of FACE 798. Draw concentric closed profiles defining the filler-neck outside diameter and the internal pouring bore. Constrain both profiles concentrically to the established +Y axis.

Dimension the neck outside diameter, bore, wall thickness, and cap-engagement diameter from the mating envelope of F012 where reliable measurements can be extracted. If the single closed BSpline face does not expose stable dimensions, use approved radiator filler-neck and cap specifications rather than assuming dimensions from the images.

Cut the inner circular profile through the upper-header wall to create a continuous fluid opening into the coolant-containing region of R01. Limit the cut to the header wall and internal coolant volume; do not extend it into F002 core panels, R02 fan guards, fan blades, or the paired F010 coolant hose fittings.

Extrude the annular outer profile upward along +Y to form the pouring neck or collar. Prefer a fused union with SOLID 0 so that the neck and upper header form one pressure-containing body. Because the source STEP is reported invalid, heal the imported body before the union; if a reliable union cannot be obtained, create the neck as a separate watertight solid with an exact coincident attachment interface to FACE 46.

Add a stepped external or internal retention interface at the upper end of the neck to suit the selected cap design. Include a planar annular sealing land and an axial stop shoulder. Use a thread, bayonet, or other positive retention feature only after the required closure standard is established.

Blend the neck root into the upper header with a pressure-compatible fillet to reduce local stress concentration. Add a small lead-in chamfer or radius at the pouring bore and cap-engagement edge to assist pouring, cap installation, and seal protection.

Check that the resulting passage is open from the top of the filler neck into the radiator header, that the neck wall is continuous and watertight, and that no residual face from the bore cut blocks the flow path.

Verify clearance in the +X, -X, +Z, -Z, +Y, -Y, and iso views. The neck must remain centered at the existing F012 location, clear of the two fan envelopes and guards in R02, and offset from F010 hose fittings and F011 corner plugs or mounts.

Run B-rep healing and validity checks after the cut and union, confirming manifold topology, positive wall thickness, no self-intersections, and no unintended modification of FACE 22, FACE 24, FACE 42, the broad core faces, or the fan-system faces.

actions.relational_constraint: The cap must be included in the filling system located on the radiator.
actions.unresolved_reference: The cap location is resolved to the existing upper filler or service closure F012, SOLID 19, FACE 798, centered over FACE 46. The existing cap should be retained if it mates correctly with the new pouring neck; otherwise it should be replaced rather than duplicated. Exact retention, pressure-rating, sealing, clearance, and grip details remain unspecified.
steps: Use R03 feature F012 and FACE 798 as the primary localization and shape reference for the cap. The model report identifies FACE 798 as the sole closed BSpline face of SOLID 19, centered near CAD z=0 and above the upper header, and the multiview images confirm its cap-like shape.

Inspect the existing SOLID 19 for watertightness, usable wall geometry, and compatibility with the newly created filler neck. If it already supplies an adequate removable closure, retain it and modify only its hidden mating interface. If it cannot provide a reliable mating interface because it is represented as one closed BSpline face, replace SOLID 19 with a new parametric cap occupying the same envelope.

Create a datum axis coincident with the pouring-neck axis normal to FACE 46 and directed along +Y. Create a radial section sketch on a plane passing through this axis and use FACE 798 as the external-envelope reference.

Sketch the cap half-profile with an outer skirt, upper crown, lower entry edge, axial stop, and internal cavity. Revolve the closed profile through 360 degrees about the filler-neck axis to create a separate removable cap solid; do not fuse the cap to R01 or the pouring neck.

Model the cap retention geometry to match the neck interface created in the first action. For a threaded design, create matching internal thread clearance and an axial stop; for a bayonet design, create matching entry slots and locking ramps. Do not select a retention type solely from the images when no engineering standard is provided.

Create an annular seal seat or gasket recess inside the cap so that the seal bears against the planar annular land on the filler neck. Maintain appropriate axial compression and radial clearance according to the selected seal and radiator operating-pressure specification.

Preserve or recreate the manually grippable flared crown visible in FACE 798. Add grip ribs, lobes, or flats only if required, maintaining clearance from the upper header and nearby frame geometry throughout cap rotation or removal.
Apply small fillets to the crown-to-skirt transition and external grip edges. Add a lead-in chamfer at the cap entrance and remove sharp internal edges that could damage the neck or seal.

Position the cap concentrically over the filler neck with its seating direction along -Y. Set the assembled axial location from the neck stop and sealing land, while retaining the cap as an independent solid corresponding functionally to R03.

Perform interference and clearance checks between the cap, filler neck, FACE 46, upper-header blends including FACE 38 and FACE 56 where locally relevant, and all nearby radiator geometry. Confirm that the cap can be installed and removed without contacting R02 fan guards or F010 hose fittings.

Validate the completed filling system in closed and cap-removed configurations. Confirm that the cap closes the pouring bore, the seal is continuously supported, the cap is positively retained, and the pouring opening is accessible when the cap is removed.
Export or rebuild the final cap as a valid watertight removable solid. Eliminate any overlap with the original SOLID 19 so that only one cap occupies the F012 location.

intention: Provide a filling system that allows the radiator to be filled or poured into and subsequently closed with a cap.
